title: Attend to the Production of Mixed Feed

lessons.title: Preparing and running grinding and batching
lessons.html:
Preparing and running grinding and batching

This module covers the hands-on work of producing mixed feed: preparing equipment, running batches, checking quality and recording. Follow your mill's SOPs at all times.

Pre-start checks

  1. Review the production schedule: products, batch sizes, number of batches and sequence (non-medicated before medicated).
  2. Confirm the correct, current formulation version is loaded in the batch system.
  3. Check production bin levels and that each bin holds its allocated ingredient.
  4. Check the hammer mill: correct screen size for the product, screen intact, hammers in good condition, magnet clean.
  5. Check the scale zero and do the daily test-weight check where required.
  6. Check the mixer is empty and clean, gate seals good, and liquid systems ready.
  7. Check micro-ingredients and premixes needed for the run: correct product, batch number, expiry date.

Grinding

  • Start the mill and aspiration before feeding.
  • Adjust feed rate to keep the motor load within the target range.
  • Take a sample to check grind visually or by sieve analysis as scheduled.
  • If the grind suddenly becomes coarse, stop and check the screen for holes.

Batching

  • Start the batch and watch each ingredient weigh in. Compare target and actual.
  • At the hand-add station, scan or check each bag against the batch ticket, weigh accurately on the calibrated scale, and add at the correct step.
  • Sign the hand-add record for each batch.
  • If an ingredient is out of tolerance or a bin runs empty, the system should hold. Report and follow the deviation procedure; do not adjust another ingredient to compensate.

lessons.title: Mixing, discharge, changeover and records
lessons.html:
Mixing, discharge, changeover and records

Mixing

  1. Let the mixer run the full dry mix time after all dry ingredients are in.
  2. Add liquids at the correct point and allow the wet mix time.
  3. Check that liquid nozzles are not blocked; blocked nozzles cause lumps and uneven fat levels.
  4. Discharge only when the surge bin below has space.

Sampling

Take samples of mixed feed at the points and frequency set in the quality plan, label them with product, batch and time, and keep retention samples as required. Look and smell: colour, texture and smell should match the product standard. Report lumps, wet spots, foreign material or unusual smells.

Changeovers and carry-over control

  • Follow the sequence plan. When moving from a medicated feed to a sensitive feed, run the specified flush batch and record it.
  • Inspect and clean mixer ribbons, discharge gate and screws where build-up occurs.
  • Clear hand-add areas of the previous product's premix bags before starting the new product.

Safety on the production floor

  • Never open mixer inspection doors while the mixer can run. Isolate and lock out first; the mixer has an interlock but do not rely on it alone.
  • Use lifting aids for heavy bags of premix; wear dust masks and gloves when handling micro-ingredients, some of which are irritants.
  • Keep walkways clear and clean up spills to reduce slips and dust.

Records

RecordContent
Batch reportProduct, formula version, target and actual weights, time, operator
Hand-add recordPremix and medicament batch numbers, weights, signature
Flush recordFlush material, quantity, where it went
Deviation reportWhat went wrong, action taken, who was informed

Key points

  • Confirm formulation version, bin contents and premixes before starting.
  • Check screens and scales; stop on sudden changes.
  • Never compensate for an out-of-tolerance ingredient by adjusting others.
  • Follow full mixing times and flushing rules.
  • Lock out before opening mixer doors and record every batch.
